meta.comment: engine.logistics (MOD-025, §8/§II.5) coarse delivery model — the STUB-FOR-BASELINE subset (FEAT-083): a single deterministic throughput/shortfall number per (district, commodity), a capacity-bounded stock shelf, and lean/fat safety-buffer tiers. The full §8 JIT depth (junction slots, truck movements, per-mode lead time, in-queue perishable expiry) is DEFERRED to after Baseline One runs; this file therefore carries none of those fields yet (GR#15: every figure below is balance data read at load time, never a Go literal in internal/engine/logistics/*.go).
meta.unitConvention: Every commodity's "unit" field states the measure its "throughput" and "holdingCostMicropoundsPerUnitPerTick" figures are PER, and is DELIBERATELY IDENTICAL to data/market.json's per-commodity "unit" field (engine.market AC-16: water/power/gas L/kWh/kWh, foodStaples/foodFresh kg/kg, fuel L, constructionMaterials tonne, consumerGoods kg, waste kg) so a tonnes-vs-slots figure is never ambiguous across the engine.market boundary (ASM-191/ASM-232). "throughput" is a plain integer count in that unit per tick (day); "shortfallFactor" is a dimensionless delivery-reliability fraction in (0,1] standing in for congestion/loss the full model would compute; "shelfLifeTicks" is in ticks/days (0 = non-perishable); "holdingCostMicropoundsPerUnitPerTick" is int64 MICRO-POUNDS per unit per tick (1 GBP = 1,000,000 micro-pounds, M0-ENG §1.2).
meta.balanceNote: All throughput/shortfallFactor/shelfLife/holdingCost/safetyBuffer figures are COARSE PLACEHOLDERS (ASM-234: unpinned balance data) chosen only to exercise the model — adjust here, never in Go source, and treat the numbers as directional pending the M2 balance pass.

lean.comment: §8 step 2 lean tier: smaller buffer, lower holding cost, higher stockout risk (AC-3).

fat.comment: §8 step 2 fat tier: larger buffer, higher holding cost, lower stockout risk (AC-3).

foodStaples.comment: Road/port-borne, storable — buffered fat against harvest lumpiness (§9).

foodFresh.comment: §6/§8 JIT poster child: short shelf life, high holding cost, lean buffer.

constructionMaterials.comment: Every build order consumes these (engine.build, US-8/AC-8) — construction competes for the junction.

waste.comment: Negative commodity (§6): export channel, never an import — the shortfall factor models export-side congestion.
